en: The medical examiner's office refused to give Nora access to non-public autopsy material.
Martin knew what to ask for instead.
"We can't reopen the case ourselves," he said. "But the public judgment quoted enough of the forensic findings."
Old injury: healed fracture of the left fifth rib.
Nora stared at the last line.
"The family doctor and dental materials introduced at trial don't mention it."
"Not mentioned isn't the same as never happened."
Nora went home that day and searched her grandmother's boxes again.
She found a hospital invoice from 1994.
The next morning she called the hospital records office. The old chart had been transferred to provincial long-term storage and could only be released under legal authorization.
She sent Martin a photograph of the invoice.
Ten minutes later he replied with two words.
I'm not guessing. I'm counting coincidences.
That evening, Martin came to the Chronicle newsroom in person.
He put a photocopy on her desk.
She stopped at the final line.
"The body had a healed rib fracture," she said.
"Lena could have had one and never known. Or the physician never recorded it."
"Not the original films. Only the wording used in court. Two molars on the body had metal restorations in positions 'substantially consistent' with Lena's dental chart."
"Fire damage destroyed part of the crowns."
"Was there ever a DNA comparison done to establish the identity of the body?"
He was silent for a moment.

"There's no request in the file for comparative DNA identification. By then, identity had been treated as sufficiently established. No one sought a family reference sample or any other comparison sample."
"So the later media stories about DNA confirmation?"
"Not supported by this file. Preserved bone, teeth, and tissue remained available. But the first actual identity comparison would be now, twenty-eight years later."
Nora closed her eyes for a second.
For twenty-eight years, headlines, documentaries, court summaries, and newspaper archives had repeated the same sentence:
Lena Zhou murdered in Alder Yard fire.
But the original foundation was this:
Someone laughed beyond the glass wall. A printer began feeding out paper. An evening editor shouted across the room that a headline needed changing.
The normality of everything was irritating.
"Then the entire case against Evan Cole collapses," Martin said.
"We have to ask who the body was."
Nora lowered her eyes to the hospital invoice beside her keyboard.
zh: 法医办公室拒绝向诺拉提供未公开的尸检材料。
“旧案重审不是我们能启动的。”他说，“但公开判决材料里引用过足够多的法医结论。”
死者：女性，年龄约二十三至二十九。
旧伤：左侧第五肋骨曾有愈合性骨折。
“庭审时牙医和家庭医生材料没有提。”
诺拉当天回家翻外婆纸箱。
她找到一张1994年的医院账单。
第二天她打电话给当年医院的档案部门。旧医疗档案已转入省级长期存储，需要法定授权才能调取。
十分钟后，他回了两个字：别猜。
她回：我没猜，我在数巧合。
当天傍晚，Martin亲自来了报社。
他把一份复印件放在她桌上。
“可能Lena本人不知道，或者医生没记录。”
“没有原始片子，只找到法庭描述。尸体的两颗臼齿有金属填充，位置与Lena牙科图表‘基本一致’。”
“当年到底有没有做过针对尸体身份的DNA比对？”
“案卷里找不到任何针对尸体身份的比较检测申请。身份当时已经被当成足够确定，没有人为这件事申请家属或其他参考样本。”
“没有那回事。至少这份案卷里没有。保存下来的只是骨、牙齿和组织样本，真正用于身份比较，是二十八年后的现在。”
二十八年来，新闻、判决书、纪录片、报纸标题全部写着同一句话：Lena Zhou murdered in Alder Yard fire。
像一块已经凝固的水泥。
但它最初的身份基础，竟然是：
办公室外有人笑，打印机吐出一摞纸，晚班编辑喊着某个标题要改。
周围的一切都正常得令人恼火。
“那Evan Cole的整个案件都会崩掉。”Martin说。
她低头看见桌边那张1994年的医院账单。
她突然觉得空气变冷了。
